hint: TRID form. Cite reg-1026-19 and reg-1026-37. Three business days after application is in 1026.19(e). Do not call it a GFE.
URLA, Fannie Form 1003 / Freddie Form 65. Not a TRID disclosure. Cite fannie-urla.
Reg Z application for TRID exists when creditor has the six items in 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3)(ii): name, income, SSN, property address, estimate of value, loan amount. Cite reg-1026-2.
1026.19(e)(2). After LE, creditor generally cannot impose a fee other than a bona fide reasonable credit-report fee until the consumer receives the LE and indicates intent to proceed.
Creditor commitment to hold a rate for a period. Industry practice plus LE lock fields in 1026.37. Do not invent a federal lock period.
Industry extension of a lock. May be a changed circumstance only if the regulation's revision rules are actually met. Do not promise that an extension always permits a revised LE.
Contractual option to obtain a lower rate before closing. Industry/pricing. Not a TRID right.
12 CFR 1026.36(d). Compensation may not be based on a term of a transaction or a proxy, other than the amount of credit. No dual compensation.
LO comp paid by the consumer. Still subject to 1026.36(d). Cannot be collected from both consumer and another person in the same transaction.
LO comp paid by the creditor. 1026.36(d) prohibits dual compensation and term-based comp.
The registry system. SAFE Act is the statute. Cite usc-12-5101 and nmls. Do not say NMLS itself issues state licenses.
12 USC 5101 and following; Reg G (1007) and Reg H (1008). Do not state current education hour counts; point to the statute and state law.
Defined in Reg Z 1026.36 and the SAFE Act. Takes an application or offers/negotiates terms for compensation.

Creditor review of credit and documentation before a property is identified. Not a TRID application until the six items, including property address, exist. Do not treat it as a commitment unless the creditor says so.
Informal payment estimate from unverified figures. Not an underwriting decision and not an application by itself.
LE page 2, Section A. Zero-tolerance bucket under 1026.19(e)(3)(i) generally. Cite reg-1026-37 and reg-1026-19.
Prepaid interest to reduce the note rate, usually shown in Section A. One point is 1 percent of the loan amount as a matter of market usage; say that is the customary meaning, not a statutory price.
Amounts the creditor contributes, including credits for a higher rate. LE/CD presentation is in 1026.37 and 1026.38. General lender credits interact with tolerance cure math.

Points that may be excluded from QM and HOEPA points-and-fees if they are bona fide under 1026.32(b)(1)(i)(E) and the related rules. Do not state the current exclusion math from memory if unsure; cite reg-1026-32 and reg-1026-43 and describe the concept.
Required when the consumer can shop for a service. Identifying information for available providers. Affects whether a shoppable fee stays in the 10 percent bucket. Cite reg-1026-19.
LE page 2, Section C. Cite reg-1026-37 and the tolerance rules in reg-1026-19.
LE page 2, Section B. Generally zero tolerance if required by the creditor. Cite reg-1026-19 and reg-1026-37.
Special information booklet for federally related purchase mortgages. Reg X 1024.6. CFPB publishes the booklet.

Reg X 1024.20. List of HUD-approved counselors provided shortly after application. Do not invent the day count if unsure; the rule says within a prescribed period — cite the section and say the timing is in 1024.20.

Reg Z uses two definitions in 1026.2(a)(6): a general business day, and a more specific rescission/CD business day (all calendar days except Sundays and legal public holidays). This distinction is the point of the entry.
When the consumer becomes contractually obligated on the loan, under state law. Not always the same day as settlement or funding. Cite reg-1026-2.
A loan originator who is not the creditor. Comp and disclosure rules in 1026.36. Not the same as a creditor.
The person to whom the obligation is initially payable, i.e. the creditor under Reg Z, when that person funds the loan. Distinguish broker and correspondent.
A lender that originates and may fund in its own name and sells the loan. Table funding is a related but different concept. Industry plus Reg X definition of table funding if relevant.
Channel in which a creditor funds loans originated by a broker. Industry practice. LO comp still applies.
Channel in which the creditor's own originators take the application. Industry practice.
Defined in Reg X 1024.2: a settlement at which a loan is funded by a contemporaneous advance of loan funds and an assignment to the person advancing the funds. Cite reg-1024-2.
Common job title for a mortgage loan originator. The legal category is MLO under SAFE and 1026.36, not the job title.
Collects documents and supports the file. Licensing depends on whether the person is an MLO under the SAFE Act definition. Do not say processors are never licensed.
A person who applies for and is obligated on the note. Contrast with co-signer and non-occupant co-borrower. URLA and Reg B.
A person who signs the note but is not an applicant in the same way. Reg B 1002.7 limits when a signature of a spouse or other person may be required.
A borrower who will not occupy. Agency guides treat income, DTI, and contribution rules differently. Cite fannie guide and do not invent an occupancy percentage.
Agency guides and title practice allow a POA in limited cases. Not a right created by TRID. Cite fannie-guide and practice-file. Do not invent witness requirements.

Fannie B3-4.3-04. Gifts from an acceptable donor for a principal residence or second home. Not allowed on investment property. Minimum borrower contribution rules differ by LTV and units. Do not restate the contribution table from memory if you might misstate it; cite the section and describe the structure.
Donor letter required by agency guides: amount, no repayment, donor identity and relationship. Cite fannie-b3-4-3-04.
Deposit under the purchase contract, credited on the CD. Source-of-funds documentation. Industry and agency asset rules.
Contract that supplies sale price, concessions, and property details used for LTV and TRID. Not a federal form.

Seller-paid costs. Interested-party contribution limits are in agency guides and differ by occupancy and LTV. Do not hardcode the current IPC grid; cite fannie-guide and say the caps are in the guide and change.

Payments by seller, builder, agent, or other interested party toward borrower costs. Agency guides cap them. Do not state a current percentage cap as if it cannot change; cite the guide and describe that caps depend on occupancy and LTV.

Borrower's cash investment. Minimums differ by program and are set in agency guides and HUD/VA/USDA rules. Do not hardcode FHA 3.5 percent as a current figure; say HUD publishes the minimum cash investment in 4000.1.
Documenting that funds to close are eligible and not undisclosed borrowed funds. Agency asset sections.
LE and CD calculating-cash-to-close table. Cite reg-1026-37 and reg-1026-38.
The creditor's written lock terms. Industry practice. The LE also discloses whether the rate is locked and until when.
15 USC 7001. Electronic records and signatures. Consumer consent requirements before electronic delivery can replace certain written disclosures.
The E-SIGN consumer consent demonstrable-ability process. Cite usc-15-7001. Do not confuse with intent to proceed.
A pre-application worksheet is not a Loan Estimate. If it looks like an LE it can create TRID problems. Cite reg-1026-19 and CFPB forms guidance. Mark the worksheet itself industry practice.

LE page 2, Section F. Prepaid interest, insurance, taxes. Generally in the no-tolerance or variation-permitted category when not required by the creditor in a zero-tolerance way. Be careful: prepaid interest can change with the per diem. Cite reg-1026-19 and reg-1026-37.
LE page 2, Section G. Deposit to start the escrow account. Cite reg-1026-37 and reg-1024-17 for escrow accounting.
RESPA definition in 1024.2. Broad list of services incident to a federally related mortgage. The hook for Section 8.
Shown on the LE and subject to 1026.36. Do not describe a legal way to pay a broker twice.
Reg Z definition: the person to whom the obligation is initially payable, regularly extending credit. Cite reg-1026-2.
The fee that may be charged before intent to proceed if it is bona fide and reasonable. 1026.19(e)(2).

Defined for revised LE purposes in 1026.19(e)(3)(iv). An extraordinary event, inaccurate information, or new information specific to the consumer or transaction. Not every change qualifies. Timing to reset charges is in that paragraph. Do not invent extra grounds.
A new LE permitted only for the reasons in 1026.19(e)(3)(iv), generally within three business days of receiving the information, and not on or after the CD when the rule forbids it. Cite reg-1026-19.

Total monthly obligations divided by qualifying income. Fannie B3-6-02 publishes manual and DU maximums that the guide can revise. Say the caps are in the current Selling Guide and cite it; you may mention that manual and DU are treated differently. Do not present a number as a statute.

Front-end ratio: proposed housing payment over income. Fannie emphasizes total DTI. FHA and VA treat housing and residual income in their own handbooks. Do not invent a universal 28 percent rule as law.
Fannie B2-1.2-01. Purchase: loan amount divided by the lesser of price or appraised value. Describe rounding only if you cite the guide. Cite fannie-b2-1-2-01.
First lien plus other financed amounts secured by the property, over value. Cite fannie-b2-1-2-01.
Home equity combined LTV includes the undrawn HELOC limit, not just the balance. Cite fannie-b2-1-2-01.
Umbrella term for DU, LPA, TOTAL, GUS. The finding is not a legal approval. Cite fannie-b3-2 and freddie-lpa and hud-4000-1.
Fannie Mae AUS. Recommendations include Approve/Eligible. Cite fannie-b3-2-01. Lender must still verify data and conditions.
Freddie Mac AUS. Do not invent recommendation names if unsure; describe risk class and eligibility and cite freddie-lpa.
FHA's TOTAL Mortgage Scorecard used with an AUS. HUD 4000.1. A refer result requires manual underwriting.
USDA Guaranteed Underwriting System. Cite usda-hb and cfr-7-3555. Do not invent score cutoffs.
Liquid assets remaining after closing, measured in months of PITIA. Fannie B3-4.1-01. Requirements vary by transaction. Do not hardcode a universal months number as applying to every loan.
Opinion of value. ECOA appraisal-copy rule is 1002.14. ATR/valuation independence is 1026.42. Agency property standards in the selling guide and HUD 4000.1. AIR for conventional.

Fannie offer to accept value without an appraisal in some cases. B4-1.4-10. Not a waiver the lender invents. Formerly called an appraisal waiver in market speech; use Fannie's current name and mention the old phrase as an alias.
Reg Z 1026.42 and the agency Appraiser Independence Requirements. No one may cause the value to be based on a desired result.
Standard data format for appraisal reports delivered to the GSEs. Cite fannie-b4-1-1-02 or fannie-guide.
The portal used to submit appraisal data to the GSEs. Cite fannie-guide.
Documenting employment and income. Fannie B3-3.2-01 and B3-3.1-01. Written VOE is not the same as verbal VOE.
Fannie B3-3.1-04. Timing is in the guide and differs for employment versus self-employment. Do not state a day count unless you describe it as guide text that can be revised and cite the section.
Third-party or document verification of qualifying income. Related to ATR documentation and agency guides.
Asset verification. Bank statements or a VOD. Cite fannie guide asset section via fannie-guide if you lack a tighter id.
Standard employment income document. Fannie B3-3.2-01. Do not invent a required stub count as law; the guide states the documentation standard.
Wage and tax statement used with pay stubs and sometimes transcripts. Agency income documentation.
Required for self-employment and certain other income. Fannie B3-3.1-02. Personal returns are Form 1040.
IRS form authorizing a transcript. Fannie B3-3.1-02. Do not call it 4506-T as the current form; 4506-C replaced it. Mention 4506-T only as a former name.
Fannie section B3-3.5. Generally a history and access to the business income. Do not invent a universal two-year rule as a statute; the guide states the history it wants and the exceptions.
Asset documentation and, in non-agency programs, sometimes income documentation. Distinguish agency asset statements from a bank-statement non-QM program.
Agency guides require sourcing deposits that are large relative to income. Do not invent the percentage threshold; cite fannie-guide and say the guide defines what must be sourced.

Funds that have been in the account long enough that the guide does not require the same sourcing. The seasoning period is guide text. Cite fannie-guide and do not state a day count as if it were a statute.
Report from Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion. Fannie B3-5.2-01. Permissible purpose under FCRA.
A score on the credit report. The representative score for the loan is a separate defined step. FCRA adverse-action score disclosure may apply. Cite fannie-b3-5-1-01 and usc-15-1681m.

Fannie B3-5.1-02. For one borrower, generally the middle of three or the lower of two. For multiple borrowers, the guide selects among the borrower scores. Describe the method and cite the section rather than paraphrasing a shortcut that might be wrong.
A credit account reported on the credit report. Agency credit history uses tradelines to measure depth of credit. Cite fannie-b3-5-2-01.
A debt with a collection. How it counts in DTI and whether it must be paid is guide- and program-specific. Do not state a universal payoff rule.
A creditor has written the debt off for accounting. It can remain collectible. Underwriting treatment is program-specific.

Waiting period after bankruptcy before a new mortgage. Fannie B3-5.3-07. Periods differ by chapter and extenuating circumstances and the guide revises them. Cite the section and do not present a single number of years as applying to every case.
Waiting period after foreclosure, deed-in-lieu, or short sale. Same section family as bankruptcy. Do not collapse all events into one number.
Fannie B3-5.3-04. Recent inquiries may require an explanation or verification that no new debt was opened.
Borrower statement addressing a credit, address, employment, or deposit question. It does not replace documentation the guide requires.
Amortizing debt with a fixed payment. Fannie B3-6-05. When a payment may be omitted because few payments remain is in the guide. Do not invent the remaining-payment count.
Credit cards and lines. If no payment is reported, guides impute a payment. Do not state the imputation percentage from memory; cite fannie-b3-6-05 and say the guide specifies the payment to use.
Income-driven payments and deferred loans have specific guide treatments. Cite fannie-b3-6-05. Do not invent the percentage of the balance used when a payment is missing.
Fannie B3-5.3-06. An authorized-user tradeline is not the same as a joint obligation. DU and manual rules differ.
State-law marital property regime. Non-borrowing spouse debts may count. Cite fannie-guide and reg-1002-6. Do not list states unless you are sure; say it depends on state law.
A spouse who is not on the note. Reg B limits required signatures. Community-property debts can still matter. Cite reg-1002-7.

Money left after debts, taxes, and the housing payment. Central to VA underwriting in Pamphlet 26-7 Chapter 4. FHA manual underwriting can use it as a compensating factor by reference to the VA table. Do not reprint the dollar chart; it is regional and household-size specific and should be read from the handbook.
A strength that can offset a weakness in manual underwriting. What counts is program-specific. Cite fannie-b3-1-01 and hud-4000-1.
A person, not an AUS approval, makes the credit decision. Fannie B3-1-01. Required documentation is usually heavier. DU Approve is not manual.
DU recommendation. Fannie B3-2-05. Meets Fannie credit risk and eligibility only if data are accurate and conditions are cleared.
DU B3-2-06. Credit risk may be acceptable but an eligibility rule failed. Not a denial by itself and not a license to deliver.
DU B3-2-07. Not an Approve recommendation. Describe it from the guide, not as an automatic denial.
DU B3-2-08. The casefile is outside what DU evaluates.
Requirements that must be cleared before documents or funding. Industry file language. Cite practice-file and fannie-b3-2-11 for DU conditions.
Industry shorthand for a condition due before the closing package is drawn. Not a regulatory category.
Industry shorthand for a condition due before the loan funds. Not a regulatory category.
Internal status meaning conditions required before closing are cleared. Not a federal status and not consummation.
Approval subject to conditions. It is not clear-to-close and not a commitment to fund if conditions fail.
Principal residence, second home, or investment. Misstatement is a serious eligibility and fraud issue. Cite fannie-guide. Do not provide advice on how to misstate occupancy.

The borrower will occupy as the principal residence. Agency guides require intent to occupy within a stated period. Cite the guide and do not invent the day count; say the guide sets the occupancy timeline.

A one-unit property occupied by the borrower for part of the year, not subject to rental controls the way a principal residence is, and not a rental investment. Guide requirements restrict rental and property type. Cite fannie-guide.
Held for rental or other income, not occupied as a principal or second home. Different LTV, reserve, and gift rules.
Principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and association dues or similar assessments. The qualifying housing payment. Cite fannie-b3-6-03.

The rate used to calculate the payment for DTI, which may differ from the start rate on an ARM or buydown. Cite fannie-b3-6-04. Do not state a universal fully-indexed or note-rate-plus formula unless you tie it to the specific product and the current guide.
Fannie B3-3.1-01. Income that is stable, documented, and expected to continue. The three-year continuance test applies only to income with a defined expiration.
Fannie B3-3.3-02. History and likelihood of continuance. Do not state a universal two-year average as a statute.
Subject property and other real estate. Schedules E, leases, and add-backs are guide-specific. Cite fannie-guide. Do not invent a vacancy factor.
Sole proprietorship income on Form 1040 Schedule C. Part of self-employment analysis. Cite fannie-b3-3-5.
Partnership or S corporation income reported on a K-1. Percentage of ownership changes the analysis. Fannie has a K-1 topic. Cite fannie-b3-3-5 and do not invent the ownership percentage cutoff.

May be grossed up under agency rules because it is not taxed. Cite fannie-guide and say the gross-up factor is in the guide. Do not hardcode a percentage if you are not looking at the current section.
A break in employment that may need an explanation. Guide treatment depends on the income type. Do not invent a maximum gap.

Fannie limits the number of financed properties and adds reserves for second homes and investment properties. Cite fannie-b3-4-1-01 and fannie-guide. The numeric cap is guide policy; say it is in the guide rather than quoting a number you have not verified in this session.
Fannie B3-4.3-05. Equity the seller gives the buyer, documented. Not the same as a cash gift. A gift of equity may not be used as reserves.
A second lien or HELOC behind the first mortgage. Included in CLTV and HCLTV. Cite fannie-b2-1-2-01.
Fannie B3-6-07. A debt paid off at or before closing may be omitted from DTI if the guide's conditions are met, including source of funds.
Debt that appears after the credit report, often through a monitoring service or a new inquiry. May require resubmission to the AUS. Cite fannie-b3-2-10 on data accuracy.
Collects dues that count in PITIA and may have to be current. Project eligibility is a separate question. Cite fannie-b3-6-03.
Agency review of the project, not just the unit appraisal. Warrantable versus non-warrantable is guide language. Cite fannie-guide. Do not invent the owner-occupancy or delinquency percentage.
A PUD is a project of individual lots with common areas. Different from a condo. Cite fannie-guide.

Built to the HUD code, not the same as modular or mobile in older usage. Titling as real property versus chattel changes eligibility. Cite fannie-guide and hud-4000-1. Do not invent width or year cutoffs.
A determination of whether the improvements are in a Special Flood Hazard Area. Triggers flood insurance if it is a designated loan. Cite usc-42-4012a and fema-flood.
Hazard insurance required by the security instrument and guides. Not the same as mortgage insurance or flood insurance. Cite fannie-guide.
Fannie B3-2-02. Electronic validation of income, employment, or assets that can replace some documents. Market name Day 1 Certainty is an alias. Validation is optional and message-specific.
Fannie B3-3.1-03. A Fannie tool for calculating certain income. Using it has guide conditions. Do not describe it as required for every file.
Can be qualifying income or a debt. Fannie B3-3.4-02 and B3-6-05. ECOA limits how the creditor treats it. Cite reg-1002-6 as well.
ECOA prohibits discounting income because it comes from public assistance. 1002.6. Documentation is still required. Fannie B3-3.4-12.
Statements, verifications, and large-deposit sourcing used for funds to close and reserves. Cite fannie-guide.

TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule. The Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure for most closed-end consumer mortgages secured by real property. Implemented in Reg Z 1026.19, 1026.37, and 1026.38. Name the main exemptions: HELOC, reverse mortgage, chattel-dwelling not secured by real property, and certain housing-assistance loans.
15 USC 1601 et seq. Implemented for these purposes by Regulation Z. Do not use TILA and RESPA interchangeably.
12 CFR Part 1026. The CFPB's TILA regulation. Overview entry that points to the part.
12 USC 2601 et seq. Settlement procedures, kickbacks, escrow, servicing. Implemented by Regulation X. TRID moved the GFE and HUD-1 for most closed-end mortgages into Reg Z.
12 CFR Part 1024. Overview entry.
15 USC 1691. Implemented by Regulation B. Prohibits discrimination on a prohibited basis.
12 CFR Part 1002. Overview entry.
12 USC 2801. Implemented by Regulation C. Data collection, not a disclosure to the borrower at application.
12 CFR Part 1003. Overview entry.
15 USC 1681. Permissible purpose, adverse action, dispute duties. Regulation V is 12 CFR 1022.
12 CFR Part 1022. Overview entry. Include risk-based pricing notice pointer.
15 USC 6801. Privacy and safeguards. Regulation P is the CFPB privacy rule. The Safeguards Rule for many nonbanks is FTC 16 CFR 314.
12 CFR Part 1016. Privacy notices and reuse limits.
12 CFR 1026.43(c) and 15 USC 1639c. Eight underwriting factors. A QM is one way to presume ATR. Do not say QM is the only legal mortgage.

12 CFR 1026.43(e). Restrictions on product features, a points-and-fees cap, and underwriting. Dollar breakpoints in the cap are adjusted annually — do not state this year's dollar cutoffs. The 3 percent tier is the regulatory cap for loans at or above the adjusted threshold; say the percentage steps and the dollar thresholds are in 1026.43 and the CFPB's annual adjustment.

The QM definition based on price and underwriting in 1026.43(e), as amended. Do not describe the expired temporary GSE QM patch as if it were still the general rule. If you mention the patch, say it ended and cite the current section.
A QM that is not higher-priced receives a safe harbor of compliance with ATR. 1026.43(b) and (e). A higher-priced QM receives a rebuttable presumption, not a safe harbor.
A higher-priced qualified mortgage is presumed to comply with ATR, and the consumer can rebut that presumption. Cite reg-1026-43 and reg-1026-35.

The QM and HOEPA calculation in 1026.32(b), used by 1026.43. What is included and excluded is specific. Bona fide discount points can be excluded only if the rule is met. Do not state this year's dollar threshold.

Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act, implemented at 12 CFR 1026.32 and 1026.34. High-cost mortgage coverage tests. APR and points-and-fees thresholds are adjusted. Do not state this year's numbers. Cite the sections.
A loan that triggers HOEPA. Additional restrictions, counseling, and ability-to-repay style limits. Cite reg-1026-32 and reg-1026-34.

Defined in 1026.35(a) by an APR spread over APOR. The regulatory spreads are 1.5, 2.5, and 3.5 percentage points depending on lien and loan size. Say those are the spreads in the regulatory text and the reader should confirm the current subsection because it has been amended. Do not confuse with high-cost/HOEPA.
1026.35(b) requires an escrow account for certain higher-priced mortgage loans, with exemptions. Do not list exemption dollar amounts that adjust; cite the section.

1026.35(c) requires a written appraisal and, for some flips, a second appraisal. Describe the existence of the rule and cite the section. Do not invent the flip price-increase percentages unless you are sure; you may omit the percentages and point to the section.
12 CFR 1026.4. The cost of consumer credit in dollars. Not the same as APR and not the same as all closing costs. Some real-estate related fees are excluded if bona fide and reasonable.
12 CFR 1026.22. The cost of credit as a yearly rate, including certain finance charges. Not the note rate. Disclosed on the LE and CD.

Reg Z disclosure of the amount of credit provided to the consumer or on the consumer's behalf. 1026.18 for non-TRID closed-end; TRID uses the LE/CD calculations. Do not equate it with the note principal.
A charge for paying early. QM limits prepayment penalties. 1026.43. Adding a prepayment penalty is also one of the CD changes that can reset the three-business-day wait under 1026.19(f)(2).

12 CFR 1026.23. For many refinances and closed-end junior liens on a principal dwelling, each consumer with an ownership interest may rescind until midnight of the third business day. Purchases and some other transactions are exempt. Use the rescission business-day definition.
Reg Z 1026.36 as a whole: compensation, qualification, and prohibited steering and loan-document practices. Distinct from the SAFE Act license.

12 CFR 1026.36(e). A loan originator may not steer a consumer to a transaction that increases originator compensation unless the safe-harbor loan options were presented. Describe the safe harbor only at a high level and cite the section.
Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. 12 USC 5531 and 5536. There is no UDAAP CFR part. Define unfair, deceptive, and abusive from the statute at a high level and do not invent elements.
12 USC 5531(c). Substantial injury, not reasonably avoidable, not outweighed by benefits. Cite the statute. Do not add a fourth element.

The CFPB uses a representation, omission, or practice that misleads or is likely to mislead a reasonable consumer, and that is material. The standard is articulated in CFPB examination and enforcement materials rather than a single CFR section. Cite usc-12-5531 and cfpb-mortgage-resources. Mark the exam-manual gloss carefully and do not invent a CFR cite.
12 USC 5531(d). Materially interferes, or takes unreasonable advantage of a lack of understanding, inability to protect, or reasonable reliance. Quote the structure, not a made-up test.
The set of ECOA and Fair Housing Act duties, plus UDAAP overlap. Not a single form. Cite ecoa, reg B, and fair housing.
Treating people differently on a prohibited basis. ECOA and Fair Housing. Includes overt discrimination and less obvious unequal treatment. Cite reg-1002-4.

A neutral policy with a disproportionate adverse effect on a prohibited basis, without a sufficient justification. It is a contested and fact-specific theory. Do not overstate that every gap is a violation. Cite the Fair Housing Act and Regulation B and flag the entry for expert review because case law moves.
42 USC 3601 and following, especially 3604 and 3605. Protected classes are not identical to ECOA. Do not merge the two lists. HUD is the primary enforcing agency.
Denying or discouraging credit in a geographic area because of the race or other protected characteristic of residents. Fair lending. Do not provide targeting advice. Cite fair housing and ECOA.
Directing a borrower to a product or neighborhood for an improper reason. Can be a fair-lending issue and, separately, a 1026.36(e) compensation issue. Keep the two doctrines distinct.
Required on designated loans secured by improved real property in a special flood hazard area. 42 USC 4012a. Coverage amount rules are statutory. Do not state a premium. Cite fema-flood.
FEMA-mapped area where mandatory purchase applies, generally zones beginning with A or V. Say 'generally' and cite FEMA rather than pretending every map panel is simple.
31 USC 5311 and following. AML program and reporting. Mortgage companies that are residential mortgage lenders or originators look to 31 CFR 1029.

Policies, controls, a compliance officer, training, and independent testing. For nonbank mortgage lenders, 31 CFR 1029.210 is the program requirement if you are confident; otherwise cite cfr-31-1029 at the part level and do not invent a subsection.

Banks have a CIP rule. Nonbank mortgage CIP expectations should not be stated as if they were the bank CIP at 31 CFR 1020.220 unless that section applies. Cite cfr-31-1029 and fincen and describe customer identification at a program level. Flag if you discuss nonbank CIP specifics.

A SAR is filed with FinCEN. Do not describe how to structure a transaction to avoid a SAR. Cite 31 USC 5318 and cfr-31-1029. Do not state a dollar threshold unless you cite the current subsection; thresholds differ by institution type. Safer to say the threshold and the confidentiality rule are in the FinCEN rule and that a SAR is confidential.
Screening parties against sanctions lists. Cite ofac. Do not invent a match-resolution procedure as law.
SAFE Act floor plus state statutes. License triggers, surety bonds, and net worth are state law. Do not state a bond amount. Cite usc-12-5104 and reg-1008 and nmls.
Reg Z 1026.24 and the MAP Rule, Reg N, 12 CFR 1014. Trigger terms, clear and conspicuous disclosures, and a ban on material misrepresentation.

Specific credit terms in an advertisement that require additional disclosures under 1026.24. Do not invent the list; name examples you are sure of (the amount or percentage of any down payment, the number of payments or period of repayment, the amount of any payment, the amount of any finance charge) and cite the section.
Regulation N, 12 CFR 1014. Mortgage Acts and Practices — Advertising. Prohibits material misrepresentations in commercial communications about mortgage products.

Reg B 1002.9. Generally within 30 days of a completed application. Content requirements include the statement of action, reasons or the right to request them, and ECOA notice. FCRA adds score and credit-agency content when a consumer report was used. Cite both.

Reg B 1002.14. Provide a copy of appraisals and other written valuations promptly upon completion, or no later than three business days before consummation, whichever is earlier. Applicant may waive the timing but must still receive the copy no later than at or before consummation. Do not shorten this into 'three days' without the promptly-upon-completion branch.

The LAR. Data fields are in 1003.4. Submission timing is in 1003.5. You may say the annual submission deadline is in 1003.5 rather than stating the calendar date, or state March 1 only if you describe it as the regulatory deadline in 1003.5 and note it can fall on the next business day. Safer: cite 1003.5 and say the annual deadline is specified there.
HMDA and Reg B monitoring information: ethnicity, race, and sex collected for government monitoring. 1003.4 and 1002.13. Taking it is required in covered cases; using it to discriminate is forbidden.

Reg X 1024.15. A person referring settlement-service business to an affiliate may receive a return on ownership if the AfBA disclosure is given, the use is not required, and the only thing of value is a permissible return. Cite reg-1024-15.
12 USC 2607 and 12 CFR 1024.14. No kickback or split of a charge except for services actually performed. Things of value are broad.
A thing of value given for the referral of settlement-service business. Illegal under RESPA Section 8. Cite reg-1024-14. Do not describe how to disguise one.
Reg X 1024.14. Broad: money, discounts, trips, free marketing, and other benefits. The definition is in the section and the official interpretations.

Regulation P. Initial and annual privacy notices, with an exception from the annual notice in some cases. Do not state that every institution must mail a full annual notice every year; the exception is real. Cite reg-1016.
FTC 16 CFR Part 314 for nonbanks. Written information-security program. Do not attribute this part to the CFPB.

12 CFR 1022.72 and FCRA. Notice when credit is on materially less favorable terms based on a consumer report. The credit-score disclosure exception exists. Cite the section and do not invent the cutoff.
FCRA 15 USC 1681b. A consumer report may be pulled only for a listed purpose, commonly a credit transaction involving the consumer. Do not suggest pulling credit without a purpose.
The 2010 Act that created the CFPB and enacted ATR/QM, LO comp amendments, and UDAAP. Cite usc-12-5531 as one anchor and describe it as the statute, not a CFR part.
The federal agency that administers Regs Z, X, B, C, V, and P for most mortgage creditors. It does not insure deposits and it is not a lender.

50 USC 3937 is the six-percent interest-rate cap on pre-service debts, upon a proper request. 50 USC 3953 addresses mortgage foreclosure protections. Do not confuse with the Military Lending Act. The six percent figure is statutory.
10 USC 987 and 32 CFR Part 232. A residential mortgage secured by a dwelling is excluded from consumer credit under 32 CFR 232.3(f)(2). Do not tell lenders to ignore SCRA because MLA does not apply.

Reg B 1002.12 is 25 months for most consumer credit and 12 months is NOT the mortgage rule — for certain mortgage applications Reg B requires a longer period. Be careful: 1002.12(b) requires creditors to retain records for 25 months generally, and for 12 months is business credit... For mortgage, I recall 25 months for most and HMDA is different (generally 3 years for the LAR in older rules, but modified). DO NOT state a retention period unless sure. Hint to the writer: cite 1002.12 and 1003.5 and say the retention period is specified in those sections. Do not quote a number of months or years.

Defined in Reg Z 1026.41. Certain Reg X and statement rules have small-servicer exemptions. Do not state the loan-count threshold; it is in the definition and should be read there. Cite reg-1026-41 and reg-1024.
A Reg Z category used for certain QM and HPML escrow provisions. The origination-count and asset limits are adjusted. Do not state this year's numbers. Cite reg-1026-35 and reg-1026-43.
Reg X concept: requiring a consumer to use a particular settlement-service provider. Relevant to AfBAs and Section 8. Cite reg-1024-15 and reg-1024-2.

A contract to pay for actual marketing services. Can be a Section 8 violation if it pays for referrals. There is no safe-harbor CFR section. Cite reg-1024-14 and cfpb-mortgage-resources. Flag for expert review.
16 CFR 681. Identity-theft detection program for creditors with covered accounts. A mortgage loan can be a covered account. Cite cfr-16-681.
12 CFR 1026.42. Misrepresenting or influencing an appraisal, and the prohibition on basing compensation on a desired value.

Stating an occupancy that is not true in order to obtain loan terms. It is fraud and a repurchase/rep-and-warranty problem. Do not explain how to conceal occupancy. Cite fannie-guide and practice-file.

Borrowers with limited English proficiency. ECOA and UDAAP do not require a Spanish closing package by themselves, but misleading English-only conduct can be a UDAAP or fair-lending problem. Do not invent a translation mandate. Cite reg-1002-4, usc-12-5531, and cfpb-spanish. Flag for expert review.
The five-page TRID closing form. 1026.19(f) and 1026.38. Delivered so the consumer receives it at least three business days before consummation. Not the HUD-1 for TRID loans.

Two different TRID clocks share this nickname: the LE within three business days after application, and the CD at least three business days before consummation. Also rescission is three business days. The entry must separate them. Use the correct business-day definition for the CD and rescission.

1026.19(f)(2)(ii): a new three-business-day wait if the APR becomes inaccurate under 1026.22, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added. Other changes may require a corrected CD without resetting the wait. Do not say every change restarts the clock.

1026.19(e)(3)(i). Charges that generally may not increase from the LE: the creditor's or broker's charges, transfer taxes, and charges paid to an affiliate or to a provider the consumer cannot shop for, with the section's exceptions. Cite the section rather than a homemade list if you might omit an exception.

1026.19(e)(3)(ii). The cumulative bucket for recording fees and for shoppable services when the consumer picks a provider on the written list. The 10 percent is in the regulation. It is cumulative, not item by item.

1026.19(e)(3)(iii). Charges that can increase without a tolerance limit, including prepaid interest, property insurance, escrow amounts, and services the consumer shops for off the written list, subject to the section. Also a changed circumstance can revise estimates.

If a charge exceeds the allowed tolerance, the creditor cures by refunding the excess, generally at or within 60 days after consummation. The 60-day cure period is in 1026.19(f)(2)(v). You may state it and cite that paragraph. A principal curtailation is one method the rule discusses; do not invent others.
The costs to close, disclosed in the LE and CD, not a single regulated number. Separate lender charges, shoppable services, taxes, prepaids, and escrow.
Amounts the seller contributes, shown in the CD summaries of transactions and in cash to close. Not the same as a lender credit. Interested-party contribution limits are a separate agency rule.

The escrow aggregate adjustment on the CD that prevents collecting more than the RESPA aggregate escrow analysis allows. Cite reg-1024-17 and reg-1026-38. It is often a negative number. Do not invent the cushion months; the RESPA cushion is in 1024.17 and is up to one-sixth of the estimated annual disbursements, which is two months. That one-sixth / two-month cushion is regulatory. You may state it and cite 1024.17.

Insures against covered title defects. Lender's policy and owner's policy are different. Shown in LE/CD services sections. Industry rate is state-regulated. Cite practice and reg-1026-37 for placement on the form.
Protects the lender's lien. Usually required. LE/CD Section B or C depending on whether the consumer can shop.
Protects the owner. Optional in many purchase transactions but often requested. On a purchase LE it is disclosed in a specific way. Do not say it is federally required.
Pricing when an owner's policy is issued at the same time as the lender's policy. State title practice, not a federal rate. Industry practice.
The person who conducts the closing and disburses. May be a title company, escrow company, or attorney depending on the state. RESPA settlement service. Not always the lender.
Interest from funding to the start of the first payment period. LE/CD Section F. Can change with the closing date. Per diem.
The daily interest amount used to compute prepaid interest. Example math must be labeled as an example. Cite reg-1026-37.
Government fees to record the deed and security instrument. In the 10 percent cumulative bucket. LE Section E. Cite reg-1026-19.
State or local taxes on the transfer. Generally zero tolerance. LE Section E. Cite reg-1026-19.
Dividing taxes, HOA dues, or rents between buyer and seller at closing. Shown on the CD summaries. Contract and local custom. Not a TRID tolerance category by that name.
The CD table comparing the LE cash to close with the final cash to close. Cite reg-1026-38.
TIP. The total interest paid over the loan term as a percentage of the loan amount, on the CD comparisons. Cite reg-1026-38. Not the APR and not the note rate.
CD page 5 comparisons: in five years, APR, and TIP. Cite reg-1026-38.
CD page 5: total of payments, finance charge, amount financed, APR, and TIP. Cite reg-1026-38.

Whether a later buyer may assume the loan at the original terms. Disclosed on the LE and CD. FHA and VA are often assumable with approval; conventional loans often have a due-on-sale clause. Do not say every FHA loan is freely assumable without credit approval.
A term allowing the creditor to demand early repayment. Disclosed on the LE and CD. Most standard first mortgages do not have one. Cite reg-1026-37.
When the payment does not cover interest and the principal increases. Disclosed on the LE and CD. Restricted for qualified mortgages. Cite reg-1026-37 and reg-1026-43.
Whether the servicer accepts payments that are less than the full amount due. Disclosed on the LE and CD. Cite reg-1026-38. The disclosure is not a promise that a partial payment cures default.
Funding and disbursement occur at the closing table, common in some states. Contrast dry funding. Industry and state practice. No federal requirement to be wet or dry.
Documents are signed and funds are disbursed later, after a review, common in some western states. Industry and state practice.

Criminal diversion of closing funds by impersonating the settlement agent. A security practice entry. Do not provide attack instructions. Tell the reader to verify wiring instructions by a known phone number. Cite practice-cfpb or cfpb-owning if it has guidance; otherwise practice-file and describe it as a fraud risk, industry practice.
The release of loan funds. May be the same day as consummation or later. Not the defined term consummation.
The seller receives a CD showing the seller's side. The buyer and seller may receive different versions. Cite reg-1026-38.
A measurement of the property boundaries and improvements. May be required by title or the lender. Not the appraisal. Industry and title practice.
The title company's commitment to insure, listing requirements and exceptions. A closing condition. Industry practice.
The mortgage or deed of trust that creates the lien. Separate from the promissory note. State law chooses which instrument. Cite practice-file.
The borrower's promise to repay. The note rate lives here. It is not the APR and not the security instrument.
A title underwriter's letter covering certain closing-agent acts. Industry and state practice. Often a shoppable or required title charge on the LE.
The buyer's inspection of the property shortly before closing under the purchase contract. Not a federal requirement and not the appraisal.
The CD signature line confirms receipt, not acceptance of the loan. Say that explicitly. Cite cfpb-cd and reg-1026-38.
LE page 1 states whether the loan has an escrow account. The initial escrow disclosure is also a RESPA document. Cite reg-1026-37 and reg-1024-17.
The set of documents signed at closing: note, security instrument, CD, and riders. Industry term. Not a single federal form.
The person responsible for receiving payments and administering the loan. Reg X servicing rules. The servicer may not be the owner of the loan.

12 CFR 1024.33. Notices and the protection of borrowers who pay the old servicer during a transition period. Do not state day counts unless you cite 1024.33 and describe them as the regulatory periods, including the 60-day late-fee protection if you are accurate. You may say: the rule requires notices and, for a period stated in 1024.33, a payment sent to the old servicer cannot be treated as late. If unsure of the numbers, do not quote them.
The goodbye and hello notices under 1024.33. Cite the section. Avoid a day count if unsure; the section states when each notice is due.
1024.33 protects a borrower who sends a timely payment to the transferor servicer for a stated period. Describe the protection and cite the section.
An account the servicer maintains to pay taxes and insurance. Reg X 1024.17. Also called impound. Not the same as earnest-money escrow at closing.
The annual analysis required by 1024.17. Determines shortage, surplus, and the new payment. Cite reg-1024-17.

When the escrow account will not have enough to pay items when due. 1024.17 allows collecting the shortage in monthly installments or, in some cases, a lump sum. Do not invent the shortage threshold for a lump-sum demand; cite the section.

When the account is over the target balance. 1024.17 requires a refund above a threshold and otherwise allows a credit. The threshold is in the section (a surplus of 50 dollars or more is refunded — this is a longstanding regulatory figure in 1024.17). You may state it only as the figure in 1024.17 and tell the reader to confirm the current text. If you do not want the risk, say the refund threshold is specified in 1024.17.
The buffer 1024.17 allows, up to one-sixth of estimated annual disbursements (two months), unless state law or the loan documents set a lower cushion. That one-sixth is regulatory.
Hazard insurance the servicer obtains when the borrower's policy lapses. 1024.37. Notice requirements and cancellation when the borrower provides proof of coverage. Do not call it mortgage insurance.

Alternatives to foreclosure: forbearance, repayment plans, modifications, and other options. Reg X 1024.41 is the procedure. The product terms come from the investor (Fannie, Freddie, FHA, VA, USDA, or a private investor).

1024.41. A complete application triggers evaluation timelines and foreclosure protections. Acknowledge-receipt timing is in the section. Do not quote day counts unless you are describing 1024.41's text (acknowledgment within 5 business days is the regulatory standard, excluding some violations). You may state the 5-business-day acknowledgment and the 30-day evaluation if you cite 1024.41 and mention exceptions.

A temporary reduction or suspension of payments. It is not forgiveness. Interest and the missed amounts are handled by the agreement. Investor rules differ. Cite reg-1024-41 for the procedure and the investor guide for the program.
A permanent change to one or more loan terms. Not a refinance and not forbearance. Investor programs set the waterfall. Cite reg-1024-41 and fannie-guide or hud-4000-1 as applicable.
An agreement to cure a delinquency by paying the regular payment plus an extra amount. Not a modification. Industry and investor rules.

Moving missed amounts to the end of the loan without capitalizing them the way a modification might. Investor-specific. Do not describe a Fannie COVID program as if it were still open. Cite fannie-guide and say the available deferral is the one in the current guide.

An FHA loss-mitigation tool that puts missed amounts in a subordinate, often zero-interest, note due at payoff. HUD 4000.1. Do not state the current maximum percentage; HUD revises it. Cite hud-4000-1.
A sale for less than the amount owed, with the investor's approval. Foreclosure alternative. Credit and waiting-period effects are guide-specific.
The borrower transfers the title to the lienholder instead of a foreclosure sale. Investor approval. Not available by federal right in every case.

The legal process of enforcing the lien after default. Judicial or nonjudicial is state law. Federal servicing rules limit the first notice or filing and dual tracking. Cite reg-1024-41. Do not describe a uniform 90-day federal foreclosure.

Proceeding with foreclosure while a complete loss-mitigation application is being evaluated. 1024.41 restricts it. Describe the restriction and cite the section rather than saying dual tracking is always illegal.

1024.41(f): a servicer shall not make the first notice or filing for foreclosure until the borrower is more than 120 days delinquent, with exceptions in the section. The 120 days is regulatory. State the exceptions exist.

12 CFR 1024.35. Written notice asserting a covered error. Acknowledgment and response timelines are in the section. The old name qualified written request overlaps. You may state the regulatory timelines if you cite 1024.35: generally acknowledge within 5 business days and respond within 30 business days, with a possible extension. Mention covered errors are listed in the section.
12 CFR 1024.36. A written request for information about the account. Separate from a notice of error. Timelines are in the section.
The older RESPA name. For loans covered by the current servicing rule, borrowers use a notice of error or a request for information. Explain the relationship. Cite reg-1024-35 and reg-1024-36.

12 CFR 1024.39. Live contact and a written notice early in delinquency. Small servicers have modifications. You may describe the 36-day live-contact and 45-day written-notice standards as the text of 1024.39 if you mention exemptions. If you are not sure, cite the section without numbers.

12 CFR 1024.40. Personnel accessible to a delinquent borrower who can discuss loss mitigation. The market says single point of contact. The rule does not require one named person in every case. Be precise.

12 CFR 1026.41. Periodic billing statement for residential mortgage loans, with exemptions including some small servicers and certain fixed-rate loans with coupon books. Do not say every mortgage gets a statement.
12 CFR 1026.20(c) and (d). Notices before the first adjustment and before later adjustments. The lookback and day counts are in the section. Cite reg-1026-20 and avoid a specific day count if unsure.
12 USC 4901 and 4902. Borrower-requested cancellation and automatic termination of borrower-paid PMI on covered mortgages. Not FHA MIP.

12 USC 4902(a). The borrower may request cancellation on the date the principal balance is first scheduled to reach 80 percent of the original value, if conditions in the statute are met, including being current and a good payment history. Do not omit the conditions. Original value is defined in the statute.

12 USC 4902(b). Automatic termination on the termination date, based on the initial amortization schedule reaching 78 percent of original value, if the borrower is current. If not current, termination occurs when the borrower becomes current. Final termination at the midpoint is also in the statute. Do not collapse this into 'PMI drops off at 78' without the current-payment condition.

A statement of the amount needed to pay the loan in full. Reg Z 1026.36 addresses payoff statements. Do not state a day count; say the timing standard and its exceptions are in 1026.36 and must be read there.
The loan is past due. Reg X early intervention and foreclosure timing use delinquency. The servicing definition is in Reg X. Do not equate one missed payment with foreclosure.
The creditor's right, after default, to declare the full balance due, if the note and state law allow it. Not the same as a demand feature on a non-defaulted loan.

Curing the default by paying the amount required to bring the loan current and stop acceleration or foreclosure, when the contract or state law allows it. Not a federal uniform right. Cite the note/state practice and reg-1024-41 only for the servicing overlay.

A person who obtains an ownership interest after the origination, such as by death or divorce. Reg X and Reg Z have successor rules. Cite reg-1024 and reg-1026-2 if the definition is there. Confirmed successors are treated as borrowers for certain servicing rules. Do not overstate that they become personally liable on the note.

The creditor does not require an escrow account. Some loans, including certain HPMLs, cannot waive escrow. A fee for waiving escrow is a product term. Cite reg-1026-35 and fannie-guide. Do not say escrow can always be waived.

1024.41 gives a right to appeal certain denials of loan-modification options when the denial is based on the complete application and the section's conditions are met. Do not say every denial can be appealed. Cite the section.
Paying the loan in full, obtaining a release of the lien, and stopping escrow collection. Related to the payoff statement. State law controls the recording of the release.
The Reg X 1024.35 process as a whole. Overview entry that points to notice of error and the covered-error list.
A mortgage that is not insured or guaranteed by FHA, VA, or USDA. It may be conforming or jumbo. Private mortgage insurance may apply above a guide LTV.
A conventional loan within FHFA loan limits and the GSE guide. Cite fhfa-cll. Do not state this year's dollar limit.
The FHFA baseline and high-cost-area limits. They change. Cite fhfa-cll and do not print a dollar figure.
A conforming loan above the baseline limit and at or under the high-cost-area limit in a designated county. Also called super conforming. Cite fhfa-cll and fannie-guide. Do not print dollars.
A loan above the conforming limit for the county. Not eligible for standard GSE delivery. Portfolio or private-investor guidelines. No single federal jumbo regulation.

A mortgage insured by FHA under the National Housing Act. HUD Handbook 4000.1. Mortgage insurance premiums change by mortgagee letter. Do not state a current MIP rate or the minimum down payment as a fixed law; say HUD publishes both in 4000.1 and mortgagee letters.
FHA rehabilitation mortgage. Limited and standard versions exist. Cite hud-4000-1. Do not state renovation caps from memory.

An FHA-to-FHA refinance with reduced documentation. Net tangible benefit is required. Cite hud-4000-1. Do not say no appraisal is always prohibited or always waived; the handbook states when an appraisal is not required.

A loan guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs. 38 USC Chapter 37, 38 CFR Part 36, Pamphlet 26-7. Guaranty is not the same as a down payment. Funding fee rules and exemptions are on VA's schedule. Do not state the current funding-fee percentage.
The amount of guaranty available to the veteran. Basic versus bonus entitlement is handbook material. Cite va-pamphlet and usc-38-3703. Do not state a dollar entitlement as current; VA publishes it.
VA document showing entitlement. Chapter 2 of Pamphlet 26-7. Cite va-pamphlet.

Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan. Pamphlet 26-7 Chapter 6. A streamlined VA-to-VA refinance. Occupancy and net tangible benefit rules are in the handbook. Do not invent seasoning numbers; cite the handbook and say seasoning is specified there.
A VA refinance that can take equity out. Different from an IRRRL. Chapter 6. Loan-to-value and seasoning are handbook rules. Do not hardcode them.
Section 502 guaranteed rural housing loan. 7 CFR 3555 and HB-1-3555. Income limits, rural eligibility, and the guarantee fee change. Do not state current income limits or fee rates.

A loan whose note rate can change with an index plus a margin, subject to caps. Disclosed on the LE product line and in ARM notices under 1026.20. The CHARM booklet is required for ARM applications under 1026.19(b). Cite reg-1026-19 and reg-1026-20.
An ARM with a fixed period and then adjustments, such as a 5/6 or 7/6. The numbers are product names. Caps are in the note. Cite reg-1026-37 for the product disclosure.
Limits on how much the rate can change at the first adjustment, at later adjustments, and over the life of the loan. Disclosed on the LE. Contract terms, not a universal federal cap.
The published rate the note uses, such as SOFR-based indexes in current notes. The old LIBOR transition is history. Do not say LIBOR is the current standard index. Cite the note and reg-1026-20.
The fixed percentage added to the index to get the rate before caps. Disclosed to the borrower. It is not the start rate.

Index plus margin, before considering the start rate or caps. Used in some qualifying and disclosure contexts. Cite fannie-b3-6-04 and reg-1026-20. Do not claim every ARM is qualified at the fully indexed rate.
Payments of interest only for a period, then amortizing payments. A QM generally cannot have an interest-only period. Cite reg-1026-43. ATR still requires qualifying on a fully amortizing payment.

A larger payment due at the end. Generally not a qualified mortgage, with limited exceptions that should be described only by citing 1026.43 rather than by inventing which small-creditor balloons still exist.
Home equity line of credit. Open-end credit under Reg Z 1026.40. TRID LE/CD do not apply. Early disclosures do. Right of rescission may apply to a principal dwelling.
A closed-end second mortgage. TRID applies if it is a closed-end consumer loan secured by real property. Rescission may apply. Different from a HELOC.

A loan that converts equity to payments or a line, generally repaid when the borrower dies, sells, or no longer occupies. Not a TRID LE/CD loan. Counseling is required for FHA HECMs. Cite hud-4000-1 and cfr-24-206. Proprietary reverse mortgages are not HECMs.

Home Equity Conversion Mortgage, the FHA-insured reverse mortgage. 12 USC 1715z-20 and 24 CFR 206. Counseling, eligibility, and principal limits are in the rule and HUD mortgagee letters. Do not state the current principal-limit factor or lending limit.
A loan that is not a QM. It still needs evidence of ability to repay under 1026.43 unless an exemption applies. Guidelines are investor-specific. Cite reg-1026-43.
The note rate does not change. The payment can still change if taxes or insurance escrow changes. Contrast with an ARM.

A subsidy, often from the seller or lender, that reduces the payment for the first years. The note rate is not permanently reduced. Qualifying may use a different rate than the bought-down payment. Cite fannie-guide. Do not state a universal qualifying rule.

Finances construction and converts to permanent financing. One-close versus two-close is product design. TRID coverage of construction is technical. Cite reg-1026-17 and reg-1026-19 at a high level and flag the entry because construction disclosure options are easy to get wrong.
A loan that includes repair costs, such as Fannie HomeStyle or FHA 203(k). Cite fannie-guide and hud-4000-1. Do not mix the program rules.

Fannie Mae's affordable product. Income limits and underwriting flexibilities are in B5-6. Cite fannie-b5-6-02. Do not state the current area-median-income percentage; Fannie can change it. Say the income limit is in the guide.
Freddie Mac's affordable product. Cite freddie-guide. Do not state the current income-limit percentage from memory.

Funds from a housing agency or nonprofit for the down payment. Can be a subordinate lien, a grant, or a deferred loan. Agency guides treat repayment terms differently. Cite fannie-guide. Not the same as a personal gift.
A government-sponsored enterprise that buys mortgages and issues guaranteed MBS. It does not originate loans to consumers. Selling Guide and DU.
A government-sponsored enterprise that buys mortgages. Seller/Servicer Guide and Loan Product Advisor. Not a retail lender.
Guarantees securities backed by government-insured or guaranteed loans. Does not buy loans the way Fannie and Freddie do and does not set FHA credit policy.

A loan a buyer may take over with the creditor's approval and, for FHA and VA, the agency rules. Creditworthiness is still reviewed. Cite hud-4000-1 and va-pamphlet. Due-on-sale is the contrasting conventional clause.

A contract clause allowing the lender to call the loan due if the property is transferred. Common in conventional notes. Federal preemption of due-on-sale enforcement is the Garn-St. Germain Act, 12 USC 1701j-3. Cite that only if you add a statute id; otherwise describe it as a contract term and cite fannie-guide. Prefer not to invent the USC section in the prose if the catalog does not have it. Catalog does not have Garn-St. Germain. Do not cite a section number. Say it is a contract clause and that federal law limits some enforcement, and flag for expert review if you mention Garn-St. Germain by name without a catalog statute.
A loan the lender keeps rather than sells to a GSE or Ginnie pool. Guidelines can be the lender's own, but ATR still applies. Industry practice plus reg-1026-43.

A refinance primarily to change the rate or term, with limited cash back. Fannie calls a version limited cash-out. The cash-back limit is in the guide. Do not hardcode the dollar limit; cite fannie-guide.

A refinance that produces cash to the borrower above the limited amount allowed on a rate-and-term refinance, or pays off debts in a way the guide treats as cash-out. Waiting periods, LTV, and seasoning are guide rules. Cite fannie-guide. Do not state a universal 12-month seasoning rule as law.
A subsidized subordinate lien from a housing agency or nonprofit, paired with a first mortgage. Fannie has a community-seconds topic. Cite fannie-guide. Do not invent the CLTV.

Insurance that protects the lender against default on a conventional loan, usually when LTV exceeds 80 percent under the guide. Borrower-paid PMI is subject to the Homeowners Protection Act. Not FHA MIP.
The borrower pays the MI premium monthly or in a financed single premium. HPA cancellation applies to borrower-paid PMI. Cite usc-12-4902.

The lender pays the MI premium and charges a higher note rate or price. HPA borrower cancellation generally does not work the same way because the borrower is not paying a PMI premium. Do not tell borrowers they can cancel LPMI at 80 percent under HPA. Cite usc-12-4901 and fannie-guide. Flag for expert review on the HPA scope sentence.
The annual mortgage insurance premium on an FHA loan, collected monthly. Rates and duration are set by HUD and change. Do not state a current rate or whether it drops off. Cite hud-4000-1.
The one-time FHA premium at closing, which may be financed. The rate changes. Do not state the current percentage. Cite hud-4000-1.

A fee that supports the VA guaranty. Some veterans are exempt, including many with disability compensation. The percentage depends on down payment, use, and loan type and is published by VA. Do not state a current percentage. Cite va-pamphlet.
The upfront fee on a USDA guaranteed loan. The rate changes. Do not state the current percentage. Cite cfr-7-3555 and usda-hb.
The annual fee on a USDA guaranteed loan, collected with the payment. The rate changes. Cite usda-hb. Do not state the current percentage.
A feature that can finance energy improvements, available in FHA, VA, and conventional forms. Do not blend the program caps. Cite hud-4000-1 and fannie-guide at a high level.
The interest rate in the promissory note. It is not the APR. On the LE it is the interest rate in the Loan Terms table.
Borrower question. Answer in plain English and point to the loan-estimate entry. CFPB Spanish: Estimación del préstamo.
CFPB Spanish: Divulgación del cierre. Point to closing-disclosure and the three-business-day rule.

term: What is the difference between APR and the interest rate?
hint: The most common comparison question. Note rate versus APR. Point to annual-percentage-rate and note-rate. Do not use a fake current market rate; example figures only.
Private mortgage insurance, not FHA MIP and not homeowners insurance. Point to private-mortgage-insurance and HPA.
Taxes and insurance account. CFPB: cuenta de depósito en garantía. Point to escrow-account. Distinguish earnest money.
Point to rate-lock. It is a contract, not a right to the lowest rate later, unless a float-down was sold.
Debt-to-income. CFPB: relación deuda-ingreso. Point to debt-to-income-ratio. Do not state a universal maximum as law.
Discount points. CFPB uses puntos. One point customarily means 1 percent of the loan amount. Point to discount-points and lender-credits.
There is no legal fixed amount. Explain categories and that the LE itemizes them. Example figures only. Point to closing-costs.
Point to pre-approval and pre-qualification. CFPB: preaprobación.
Point to earnest-money. It is a contract deposit, usually credited at closing.
CFPB style: pago inicial. Point to down-payment. Program minimums change and are not one number.

term: Can I use gift money for the down payment?
hint: Often yes on a principal residence, with a gift letter and transfer evidence, subject to the guide. Not a universal yes for investment property. Point to gift-funds.
Point to cash-to-close. It is not only the down payment.
Point to title-insurance, lender's policy, and owner's policy.

RESPA Section 9, 12 USC 2608, prohibits a seller from requiring a particular title company as a condition of the sale in a covered transaction, with liability for damages. The catalog does not have 2608. Do not cite 12 USC 2608 unless you only describe the rule in prose without a fake catalog id, and cite respa at the act level (usc-12-2601) plus reg-1024. Actually 2608 is real. You may explain the rule in prose as RESPA's rule against a seller requiring a title company, and cite usc-12-2601 and reg-1024. Avoid inventing a subsection. Flag for expert review so the Section 9 citation can be confirmed. Also the buyer often can shop, which affects the 10 percent tolerance.
CFPB: tasación. It is for the lender, not a home inspection. Point to appraisal.

term: What if the appraisal is lower than the price?
hint: The LTV uses the lower of price or value on a purchase. Options are renegotiate, bring cash, or a reconsideration of value. Do not promise a second appraisal will be ordered. Point to loan-to-value-ratio and appraisal.
The lender's risk decision. Point to manual-underwriting and automated-underwriting-system. It is not the same as pre-qualification.

term: Why was my loan conditionally approved?
hint: Point to conditional-approval and underwriting-conditions. Conditional is not clear to close.

term: Which debts count in my DTI?
hint: Point to debt-to-income-ratio, installment-debt, revolving-debt, and student-loans. Authorized-user and omitted debts are nuances.
HPA borrower-requested cancellation and automatic termination. Not MIP. Point to the HPA entries. Do not promise cancellation at 80 percent without the statutory conditions.
Separate the CD waiting period, the LE timing, and rescission. Point to three-business-day-rule.

term: Why did my closing costs change?
hint: Tolerances and changed circumstances. Point to zero-tolerance, ten-percent-tolerance, changed-circumstance, and tolerance-cure.
CFPB servicing language: administrador del préstamo. The company you pay may not own the loan. Point to mortgage-servicer and servicing-transfer.

term: What if I cannot make my mortgage payment?
hint: Contact the servicer, ask about loss mitigation, and do not ignore mail. Point to loss-mitigation and forbearance. This is not legal advice for a particular default.
A pause or reduction, not forgiveness. Point to forbearance.

term: What is the difference between FHA and conventional?
hint: Insurance, down payment source, MIP versus PMI, and guidelines. Do not state current MIP or a minimum down payment percentage. Point to fha-loan and conventional-loan.
Point to adjustable-rate-mortgage, arm-caps, arm-index, and arm-margin. The payment can change.
Above the conforming limit. Point to jumbo-loan and conforming-loan-limit. Do not state the current limit.
Open-end credit line. CFPB describes a línea de crédito con garantía hipotecaria. Not a closed-end second. Point to heloc.
Point to reverse-mortgage and hecm. Counseling, occupancy, and repayment events. Not free money.

term: What documents will the lender ask for?
hint: Income, assets, credit, and identity. Point to pay-stub, form-w-2, tax-returns, and bank-statements. The AUS findings control the actual list.

term: How do I avoid wire fraud at closing?
hint: Verify wiring instructions using a phone number you looked up, not one in an email. Do not include attack steps. Point to closing-wire-fraud.

term: Can I cancel the loan after I sign?
hint: Only if the right of rescission applies. Purchases generally cannot be rescinded. Point to right-of-rescission. Signing the CD is not acceptance.

term: What is the difference between a co-signer and a co-borrower?
hint: Point to co-signer, co-borrower, and non-occupant-co-borrower. Reg B signature rules.
